text: Not bones in a museum. Not a movie. Living, breathing giants… sharing the planet with you.
To see how, we have to go back sixty-six million years.
A rock about ten kilometres wide is racing towards Earth at twenty kilometres per second.
In our history, it hits. Three out of every four species vanish.
But Earth moves fast through space. If that rock had arrived just a few minutes later… it would have missed.
One kilometre. Across the river, a herd of long-necks keeps on eating, as if nothing happened.
Forty metres. Triceratops, around ten tonnes each, wade in to drink.
Back then, our ancestors were tiny. Small furry mammals, hiding in the ferns.
Most scientists think we would never have appeared at all.
But imagine we did. And imagine we tried to keep them… behind a fence.
